## Terms used below

- **Record:** the stored summary of one conversation (name, times, counts, where it came from). One
  per conversation, in the DynamoDB table.
- **Row:** one stored message, or one *note*, in the same table. Flags live on the message's row.
- **Session:** a run of one conversation's messages with no pause of 15 minutes or more. Sessions
  are stored with fourteen counts each, so the page can draw the Calendar without reading messages.
- **Branch / pruning:** a conversation in the export is a tree; editing a message starts a new
  branch. The server keeps the path to the latest message and *prunes* (drops) the branches it
  replaced, leaving a **note** row where each was. A replaced branch long enough to matter is
  instead kept as a conversation of its own.
- **Unknown time:** a message without a `created_at`. It is stored with the date 1970-01-01 as a
  marker meaning "unknown".
- **Time limit (work budget):** each server request does at most about 9 seconds of work, then
  answers with what it has.
- **Part / cursor:** an answer cut short by the time limit is one *part*. It carries a *cursor*,
  an opaque marker of where to carry on, which the page sends back to get the next part.
- **Data version:** a number on the user's record that rises whenever their data changes. A page
  reading several parts checks that it stays the same, and starts over if it changes.
- **Scan:** the server's pass that sets the automatic flags (caps, critical, angry) on your
  messages.
- **Slimming:** the page, before uploading, drops what the server doesn't keep from the export
  (63.5 MB → 9.3 MB for your export) and compresses it (→ 2.8 MB). This runs in a **Web Worker**,
  a background thread of the page, so the page stays responsive.
- **Test levels:** *backend tests* are Rust tests of the server; *page unit tests* run the page's
  JavaScript in Node with stand-ins for the browser; *browser tests* (Playwright, in [e2e/](../../e2e/))
  drive the real page in Chrome against a real local server.
- **Coverage:** the share of code lines that at least one test runs.
- **Pre-existing:** present before this work began (before commit `53491ed`).

## Bugs found and fixed

### B1. A message from a later file could be mistaken for a revived branch

- **What:** when a later export of a conversation contained a message inside the time range
  already stored, processing treated it as a *revived branch* (a branch pruned earlier that a later
  export continues). That could replace stored messages with it.
- **Fix:** a revival must now actually replace something. Otherwise the plan's time rule (Q18)
  decides what is added. See [`plan_merge`](../../backend/timeline-core/src/merge.rs#L69).
- **Found by:** the new processing tests. Commit `a88ccd0`.

### B2. After two uploads raced, the conversation's record could undercount its rows

- **What:** two files processed at once can both try to update the same conversation. The record
  is written conditionally, so one writer loses and redoes its merge.
- **The bug:** on the redo, it saw the winner's rows as already stored. It then left the record's
  message count lower than the rows actually stored.
- **Fix:** whenever the record and the rows disagree, the record is brought into line with the
  rows. Commit `a88ccd0`.

### B3. A conversation with a message of unknown time lost that message

- **What:** pruning keeps the path to the latest message. A message of unknown time sorted as the
  oldest, so it was pruned away as if it were a replaced branch.
- **Fix:** a conversation with any message of unknown time is now left whole, not pruned; see
  [branches.rs](../../backend/timeline-core/src/branches.rs#L18). This is also choice
  [O14](#o14-a-conversation-with-any-message-of-unknown-time-is-not-pruned). Commit `a88ccd0`.

### B4. The annotated download left out conversations with no messages

- **Fix:** the download's last part now adds them. Commit `a88ccd0`.

### B5. Review no longer highlighted a session's rows

- **What:** clicking a session bar or a flag icon on the Calendar or the Conversations tab used to
  open Review with that session's messages highlighted.
  - The new page lost this because sessions now arrive as counts, without their messages' ids, so
    the page had nothing to highlight.
  - Three committed browser tests failed on it.
- **Fix:** the page now picks the rows to highlight from the rows the server sends: all of your
  messages for a session click, or those with the clicked flag in effect for a flag click. It waits
  until a part actually contains such a row.
  - See [`showHighlights`](../../frontend/ui/views/review.js#L418) and the callers in
    [calendar.js](../../frontend/ui/views/calendar.js#L109) and
    [conversations.js](../../frontend/ui/views/conversations.js#L285).
  - Commit `2359ce0`, with a new page unit test.
- **Related choice:** [Q6](#q6-should-clicking-a-flag-icon-filter-review-to-that-flag).

### B6. A failed read-back after saving a file's details left Describe

- **What:** after you press Done on Describe, the page saves the details and then reads the
  timeline again. If that read failed, the new page showed the error in the loading box and left
  the Describe page.
  - The committed browser test "a save whose details can't be read back stays on Describe and says
    so" expects the old behaviour.
- **Fix:** a failed read-back now closes the loading box, stays on Describe, and shows "Could not
  read your files' details: …" there. See [`readBackFailed`](../../frontend/ui/page-flow.js#L222).
  Commit `c4ba263`.
- **Related test change:** [T1](#t1-a-new-page-unit-test-was-changed-to-expect-the-opposite-of-what-it-first-checked).

### B7. A batch's files could be sent out of order

- **What:** each file of a batch is now prepared in its own worker. Whichever finished preparing
  first was sent first, so a small second file could overtake a large first one.
  - The committed browser test "Stop with one file processed and one still sending" assumes the
    first file is sent first. It failed in 2 of the 4 runs that included it.
- **Fix:** files are still prepared at the same time, but each waits to start sending until the
  file before it has started (or failed, or been stopped). See
  [load-flow.js](../../frontend/ui/load-flow.js#L285). Commit `a1635fe`.
  - The new page unit test for this fails without the fix (checked).

### B8. Two error handlers in Review dropped errors silently

- **What:** when a newer Review request replaced an older one and the older one then failed, its
  error was dropped with no log. That breaks your no-silent-swallow rule.
- **Fix:** the error is now logged as information ("a replaced page request stopped: …"); see
  [review.js:207](../../frontend/ui/views/review.js#L207) and
  [review.js:162](../../frontend/ui/views/review.js#L162). No message is shown on screen, since that
  request no longer matters. I made this change before committing the page agent's work, so it is
  in the page's first commit, `8757068`, not a separate one.

### B9. Four browser tests passed without testing anything

These tests still intercepted the old timeline download (`GET /export` on page load), which the
page no longer makes, so their setup did nothing and they passed regardless. §10b approved
changing each one.
- **"…signed in in the same tab…"**
  ([cognito-login.spec.js](../../e2e/cognito-login.spec.js)) and the `slowExport` helper in
  [views.spec.js](../../e2e/views.spec.js): they held back the download so the loading box could be
  seen. They now hold back `GET /sessions`.
- **"a session that cannot be fetched on reload…"** ([views.spec.js](../../e2e/views.spec.js)): it
  now fails `GET /sessions`.
- **"a file bigger than axum's default 2MB body limit still uploads"**
  ([upload-flow.spec.js](../../e2e/upload-flow.spec.js)): slimming shrank the file well under 2 MB,
  so the server's size limit was never reached.
  - It now opens the page with `&upload=unslimmed`, so the file is sent as it is.
  - It checks that the bytes handed to the upload request equal the file's 2,646,984 bytes.

Commit `22b1d15`.

### B10. The API template never routed PUT, so editing details could not work on AWS

- **What:** [infra/template.yaml](../../infra/template.yaml#L396) had no PUT route to the API, and its
  CORS rules (which browser origins may call which methods) did not allow PUT.
  - Editing a file's or conversation's details uses PUT, so it could never have worked on the
    deployed stack.
- **Fix:** route and CORS added (commit `e34cedd`). See also
  [T5](#t5-the-template-test-now-expects-put-among-the-allowed-methods).

### B11. The processing measurement example was already broken

- **What:** [examples/measure_processing.rs](../../backend/timeline-api/examples/measure_processing.rs)
  never recorded the upload's facts before processing, so it failed.
  - This was broken before this work began.
- **Fix:** it now records them.

### B12. The core README described the old ports

- **What:** the core README's module table and diagram predate this work.
- **Fix, partial:** the module table and the port table now list the new modules and ports, and the
  diagram gained the new methods of the ports it already showed (commit `6784c3e`).
- **Still missing:** the diagram does not show `SessionStore`, `UserRecordStore` or `AnalysisStore`,
  nor `UploadOutcomeStore`'s newer methods such as `record_processing_progress`.

## Decisions for you

### Q1. How to deploy the dev stack, which today serves the public address

**Facts (observed 2026-10-06):**
- `timeline-dev` is the only application stack in the account.
- Its CloudFront distribution `E6MWRB0WWMX8K` (CloudFront is Amazon's content-delivery network,
  which serves the page) answers for **howangryami.telotrope.ai**, with the public certificate.
  That name resolves to this distribution.
- The committed [infra/samconfig.toml](../../infra/samconfig.toml) gives dev the name
  **dev.howangryami.telotrope.ai** and a different certificate. It was committed after the last dev
  deploy (2026-10-02 22:01 UTC).
- I made a trial deploy, answering "no" at its prompt; its change set was deleted and nothing was
  applied. The planned changes it listed:
  - removing the MessageFlags table, which I counted at 0 items first, so nothing would be lost;
  - adding the PUT route;
  - updating the functions;
  - changing the sign-in client and the distribution to the new name.

**So a deploy today must do one of:**
- **(a) Deploy as committed.** The site moves to dev.howangryami.telotrope.ai, and
  howangryami.telotrope.ai stops working until something else serves it.
- **(b) Keep today's name** (`scripts/deploy.sh dev PageDomain=howangryami.telotrope.ai
  PageCertificateArn=<public certificate>`). The new API replaces the one under the live page.
  The deploy script also publishes the new page in its last step, so the page and the API would
  match, but the public address would then show this new, partly tested version.
- **(c) Something else**, such as creating a separate public stack first.

**Also needed for the AWS measurements:** the page signs in on AWS through Cognito (Amazon's
sign-in service), and the measurement script only knows local development's sign-in. Either:
- **(i)** I create a temporary user in the dev pool and delete it after the run, along with that
  user's stored data; or
- **(ii)** you sign in and run the upload yourself while I read the logs.

**Waiting on this:** step 12's AWS measurements, at 512 MB and at 1,769 MB of processing memory.

### Q2. May the activity-inventory test allow the upload worker's message events?

- **The test:** [activity-inventory.test.js:67](../../frontend/tests/activity-inventory.test.js#L67)
  lists every kind of event the page listens for. It fails if any kind is not covered by the
  activity recorder (the code that logs your clicks and views).
- **Why it fails:** a Web Worker can only send results back through `message` events. The page
  now listens for `message`, `error` and `messageerror` in
  [infra/upload-preparer.js](../../frontend/infra/upload-preparer.js), and the worker listens for
  `message` in [workers/prepare-upload.js](../../frontend/workers/prepare-upload.js). These are
  not user actions, so recording them would be wrong.
- **Proposed fix:** allow those three kinds only on a receiver named `worker` or `self`, the same
  way the test already allows the upload request's own events on a receiver named `xhr`. This
  loosens a committed test, so it needs your approval.
- **I rejected** setting the handlers as properties (`worker.onmessage = …`) to slip past the test's
  pattern. That would hide the listeners from the check rather than satisfy it.

### Q3. May the sessions-table title test look only at the Sessions title?

- **The test:** [screen-flow.spec.js:558](../../e2e/screen-flow.spec.js#L558) checks that
  `#convDetail .table-title` reads "Sessions".
- **Why it fails:** the plan's §4 added a Files table to an open conversation, titled "Files" with
  the same style class. The check now finds two titles, and Playwright refuses an ambiguous match.
- **Proposed fix:** check the first title, or the title above the sessions table specifically.
  The page's behaviour is as planned; only the test's selector is too broad.

### Q4. May the show-switches test wait for Claude's replies?

- **The test:** [views.spec.js:599](../../e2e/views.spec.js#L599). At line 627 it ticks "Claude's
  replies" and counts reply rows *immediately*, without waiting:
  `expect(await replies.count()).toBeGreaterThan(0)`.
- **Why it fails:** under the plan (§5), replies are no longer in the page. Ticking the box asks
  the server for them, so they arrive a moment later. The test passes only when the server
  answers before Playwright counts.
- **Proposed fix:** `await expect(replies).not.toHaveCount(0)`, which waits up to 5 seconds.

### Q5. Should reviews on pruned messages be kept?

- **Observed:**
  - The raw export holds 561 reviews (your `_claude_timeline_user` marks).
  - The processing before this work stored 538.
  - The new processing stores 536.
- **What I found, counting the raw file with Python:**
  - 27 reviewed messages are off the path to their conversation's latest message, so pruning does
    not keep them on that conversation.
  - 22 of them are in "Starting a government contracting business". The server stored 118
    conversations from the file's 117, so one branch was most likely kept as a conversation of its
    own, and these 22 are probably in it. I inferred this from the counts; I did not check the
    stored rows.
  - The other 5 are in branches pruned to notes, and their reviews are not kept anywhere.
  - All 27 reviews say "none of the three flags".
- **Not traced:** why the difference from the old 538 is exactly 2. The old processing dropped 23
  reviews along with the repeated sends it removes, and the two removals overlap in ways I have not
  worked out. The cheapest test: compare stored reviews per conversation against the raw file.
- **Question:** should a review on a message that pruning drops be kept, for example on its note?
  Today it is lost.

### Q6. Should clicking a flag icon filter Review to that flag?

- **Before this work:** clicking a flag icon opened Review on the session with the flag menu set
  to "All", with the flagged messages highlighted.
- **Now:** the page agent made it set the flag menu to the clicked flag, so only flagged messages
  show. Its new page unit tests expect this. The old code carried a comment saying, on purpose, that
  a flag click should *not* filter to that flag, so the agent reversed a stated decision.
  - The older browser tests expect highlighted rows. With [B5](#b5-review-no-longer-highlighted-a-sessions-rows),
    both now hold: the filter is set *and* the rows are highlighted.
- **Question:** keep the filter, or go back to "All" with highlights? Going back means changing the
  agent's new unit tests in [timeline-view.test.js](../../frontend/tests/timeline-view.test.js),
  which needs your approval.

### Q7. Per-function limits on which fields each server function may change

- **The plan:** §3 says each function's AWS permission should name the row fields it may change.
  The scan's function may change automatic flags only; flag saves may change your flags only.
- **Not done, because it would separate nothing:** one function (the API) runs both the scan and
  your flag saves, and processing writes your reviews. Per-function field limits would give the
  API both sets of fields anyway.
- **What does protect them today:** the code's types, in two port traits. `AutoFlagWriter` can
  write only automatic flags, and `UserFlagWriter` only yours.
- **Question:** accept that, or split the scan into its own function so the permission limit
  means something? Splitting adds a function and its deployment cost.

answer each as approve or revert.

## Choices Claude made where the plan was silent

Each is in effect now and can be changed. "(page agent)" marks choices made by the second agent.

### O1. Review's time order is exact, by walking groups of overlapping sessions

Review lists messages by time across conversations. Sessions are stored by conversation and
start, and two conversations' sessions can overlap in time. So the server reads sessions in
*groups* whose time spans overlap, reads each group whole, and sorts its messages by time, then
conversation, then id.
- A Calendar-day view instead walks conversations by name.
- A cursor names a group's first session and the last message done.

### O2. What a request for Review messages carries

- **The page sends:** the cursor, how many messages matched so far, how many rows it wants, and
  whether to keep counting after the rows are filled.
- **The server answers with:** rows, the match count, the starting cursors of any new pages of 50
  it passed, and the next cursor.

### O3. Messages of unknown time match a session's span, never a Calendar day

- **Session or analysis span:** a message of unknown time matches it through the session it
  belongs to.
- **Calendar day:** it never matches, since its day is unknown.
- **A conversation placed by its start and end:** every message matches any span overlapping that
  session.

### O4. Notes appear in Review only with the flag menu on "All" and no search

A note marks where a replaced branch was pruned. It has no flags and no text to search, so it
shows only when nothing is being filtered.

### O5. A new "USER" row holds your data version and totals, in the conversations table

- **The plan:** it said these go on "the user's existing record", but no such record existed.
- **What I did:** created a row with sort key `USER` in the conversations table. I did not use the
  unused UsersTable, because no code reads that table, and processing would have needed a new
  setting and a new permission for it.

### O6. The annotated download comes inside the reply, in parts

Each `GET /export` reply carries one part of the file as text, at most 4 MB, plus that part's flag
handles. The page joins the parts and saves the file. It no longer goes through a temporary S3
object and a download address. See also [T6](#t6-the-export-test-no-longer-follows-a-download-address).

### O7. Which files are kept from a conversation

Kept:
- files Claude *presented* (`present_files`);
- widgets;
- your attachments.

Not kept: a file Claude created but never presented.

### O8. A branch kept as its own conversation is named in UTC

The name is "{name}: earlier branch from 2026-06-21 16:38 UTC". The server doesn't know your time
zone.

### O9. Your data version and totals are recounted after each upload, not added to

Recounting means a retried or repeated upload cannot push the totals off. See
[`record_totals`](../../backend/timeline-storage/src/dynamo/user_record_rows.rs#L94).

### O10. One step of the time limit is one row read

Tests count steps instead of time. Each row the walk reads, Claude's rows included, is one step.
When a session ends exactly at the limit, the cursor names the next session with nothing yet done
in it.

**Correction (2026-10-07):** with "Claude's replies" on, the reply to each row shown is read
*after* the walk, by [`attach_replies`](../../backend/timeline-api/src/routes/messages.rs#L252):
one read per row, at most 50, and none counts against the time limit. That cost is fixed (it does
not grow with your data), but this entry previously said replies were included. See
[P9](#p9-claudes-replies-are-read-outside-the-time-limit).

### O11. Processing writes 8 conversations at a time

See [processing.rs:60](../../backend/timeline-api/src/processing.rs#L60). Each conversation's rows
are written in parallel batches. The per-step durations in the processing log line are therefore
summed over conversations, and can exceed the run's wall-clock time.

### O12. The download writes a message's parent only when known

A downloaded file uploaded again therefore keeps its conversations whole, instead of being pruned
by guessed parents.

### O13. A pruned branch's notes can form a session with no messages

Notes count as activity (§4d). Notes of a replaced or revived path far in time from other activity
therefore form a session of their own, with 0 messages.

### O14. A conversation with any message of unknown time is not pruned

See [B3](#b3-a-conversation-with-a-message-of-unknown-time-lost-that-message). Its latest message
can't be determined.

### O15. A revival must replace something

See [B1](#b1-a-message-from-a-later-file-could-be-mistaken-for-a-revived-branch).

### O16. `GET /export` still issues flag handles

A *flag handle* is a signed token that lets a flag save prove it names a real message. §10b's
wording ("`GET /export` still does too") was taken literally.

### O17. flate2's compression backend is zlib-rs

The gzip library flate2 (MIT or Apache-2.0) uses zlib-rs, under the Zlib licence. That licence is
permissive, but it isn't one of the four your rule names (MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, ISC). Please
confirm it is acceptable.

### O18. A test hook in the page: `?upload=unslimmed` sends files unslimmed (page agent)

See [`sendsUnslimmed`](../../frontend/ui/load-flow.js#L73). It exists so the 2 MB browser test can
reach the server's size limit. A user who adds it to the address gets the old, slow upload. Files
the worker can't slim are also sent as they are, and the server then reports what is wrong.

### O19. Slimming keeps the file's outer shape (page agent)

A bare list stays a list, and a saved timeline file stays wrapped with its format version.
- **Why:** the server removes repeated sends only for bare lists.
- **What it drops:** `_claude_timeline_auto`.
- **What it keeps:** the fields the server reads. It never adds a field.

### O20. A part holds at most 1,000 records or 2,000 sessions

See [conversations.rs:37](../../backend/timeline-api/src/routes/conversations.rs#L37) and
[sessions.rs:28](../../backend/timeline-api/src/routes/sessions.rs#L28). The time limit alone would
let a user with very many conversations get one answer over AWS's 6 MB limit. At these caps a part
is about 1 MB.

### O21. After a flag save, only that message's session is refreshed (page agent)

- **What the page does:** it takes the counted session from the save's reply and asks for Review's
  current page again from its starting cursor, counting again.
- **What it does not do:** read all sessions again.

### O22. The timeline is read when Describe is left, not while it is open (page agent)

Describe can change a conversation's start and end, which moves its sessions. So the timeline is
read after Describe closes, and again after details are saved.

### O23. Review loads only when shown (page agent)

- **When it loads:** on a tab click, an address or an entry point, not when the timeline opens.
- **Search:** waits for a 300 ms pause in typing.
- **Short parts:** when a part arrives with fewer than 50 rows, the page keeps asking until the
  page is full.
- **Back and Next:** enabled only for pages whose starting cursor is known.

### O24. A Calendar day is sent as local midnight to the millisecond before the next midnight (page agent)

The server's span includes both ends, so ending at the next midnight would include its messages.

### O25. The "may have been changed later" mark follows the server's rule (page agent)

A command marks every earlier file creation whose path or file name it mentions. This matches
[kept_files.rs](../../backend/timeline-core/src/kept_files.rs).

### O26. One shared progress bar component (page agent)

`createProgressBar` in [status-indicators.js](../../frontend/ui/widgets/status-indicators.js) is
used for the load screen, Review, Analytics, the annotated download and a conversation's files.
The processing wait keeps its own clock wording and adds bytes read, then conversations written.

### O27. The new bars record nothing in the activity log (page agent)

Review's, Analytics', the download's and the files' bars show progress but log no "shown" events.
- **Why:** the list of places that may log is fixed by a committed test, `SHOWN_PLACES` in
  [activity-event.test.js:160](../../frontend/tests/activity-event.test.js#L160).
- **The load bar:** it logs each of its new messages once.
- **To log the new bars too:** that test would have to change.

### O28. Links between a note and the conversation it became (page agent)

A note's "kept as" link, and a conversation's details, link to `#conversations/<index>`. The
Conversations tab shows "kept as its own conversation" links in both directions.

### O29. Opening a listed file opens Review on its message (page agent)

Review opens on the session holding the message. Claude's replies are turned on if Claude
presented the file, and the row is highlighted.

### O30. Source-map lines removed from the vendored parser (page agent)

Each `//# sourceMappingURL=` line was deleted from
[vendor/streamparser-json/](../../vendor/streamparser-json/).
- **Why:** the maps are not vendored, and Node's coverage report fails on a file that names a map
  it can't read.
- **Recorded:** in that folder's README, with checksums taken after the change. The vendored files
  are therefore not byte-identical to the published package.

### O31. Limits the plan did not set

Each of these numbers was chosen in the code, and the plan gives none:
- **3 restarts** when the data changes while a multi-part read runs, before the page gives up:
  [parts.js:14](../../frontend/core/parts.js#L14),
  [timeline-load.js:25](../../frontend/ui/timeline-load.js#L25) and
  [review.js:29](../../frontend/ui/views/review.js#L29) (page agent).
- **5 redos** of a write that lost a race to another writer:
  [metadata.rs:51](../../backend/timeline-api/src/routes/metadata.rs#L51), and the same in
  processing.
- **200 sessions** per storage read in `GET /sessions`.
- **A search over 200 characters is cut to 200**, not refused
  ([message_filter.rs:27](../../backend/timeline-core/src/message_filter.rs#L27)). The plan says
  "1–200 characters".
- **Session keys pad the session number to six digits** (`SESS#{conversation}#000001`). The plan
  wrote `SESS#{conversation}#{n}`.

## Problems found

### P1. Node 18 is the shell's default; the page's tests need Node 20

`node` on this machine's default PATH is v18, under which one page test fails (it needs the global
`crypto`). The package asks for Node 20. All runs used
`~/.nvm/versions/node/v20.20.2/bin`. Nothing was changed on the machine.

### P2. The disk filled during the work

`backend/target/` had grown to about 30 GB. I deleted `target/debug` and the coverage build
directory, and they were rebuilt as needed. 8.3 GB was free at the last check, and the deploy
script needs 3 GB.

### P3. Another timeline-api is listening on port 3000

The browser tests and the measurements used their own ports (3123, and 3917/8917). I did not touch
or identify the server on 3000. If it is yours from an earlier session, it is running code of
unknown age.

### P4. Local timing quirks noted in the measurement analysis

These are explained in [the measurement analysis](2026-10-06-load-only-what-the-page-shows-measurements.md),
and listed here so you can track them by ID:
- **P4a:** locally, processing happens inside the upload request, so the page cannot time it
  separately.
- **P4b:** the local scan slowed from 291 ms to 404–414 ms as other users' rows accumulated in the
  in-memory store, and returned to 265 ms after a restart. The page-side part of the variation is
  not traced.

### P5. The dev stack and its committed settings disagree

See [Q1](#q1-how-to-deploy-the-dev-stack-which-today-serves-the-public-address).
- **The disagreement:** the deployed stack still has the public address, while
  [infra/samconfig.toml](../../infra/samconfig.toml) says otherwise.
- **The deployed parameters:** they also include `RecordActivity=on` and `LogRetentionDays=7`.
  - `RecordActivity` defaults to "on" in the template, so it would not change.
  - `LogRetentionDays` was not compared with the template's default.

### P6. The live public page will break whenever the backend is deployed alone

The page at howangryami.telotrope.ai asks for the old timeline download on load. Any deployment
of the new API without publishing the new page to the same address breaks it. `scripts/deploy.sh`
publishes both together, so this risk applies only to a partial or manual deployment.

### P7. A pending highlight can outlive the jump that asked for it

Found by an agent reading the code, then checked by me in the code; not tested.
- **What:** [B5](#b5-review-no-longer-highlighted-a-sessions-rows) keeps a requested highlight
  until a part of Review's answer holds a matching row.
  - Changing the flag menu or the search box starts a new query through
    [`showFirstReviewPage`](../../frontend/ui/views/review.js#L254), which does not clear it.
- **Effect:** if the jump never showed a matching row, the next unrelated query flashes rows.
  - Example: a session holding only notes ([O13](#o13-a-pruned-branchs-notes-can-form-a-session-with-no-messages))
    has no message of yours to flash.
- **Proposed fix:** clear both highlight values in `showFirstReviewPage`. This is my bug; not
  fixed, since this request was for documentation only.

### P8. Conversation records written before this work no longer load

- **What:** [conversations_table.rs](../../backend/timeline-storage/src/dynamo/conversations_table.rs#L333)
  now requires the `version`, `untimed`, `branch_of` and `branches` fields. An older record lacks
  them and is reported as damaged; the error's text says to clear the rows and upload again.
- **Effect today:** none. I counted the dev stack's conversations table on 2026-10-07: 0 items.
- **Still matters:** any other table holding older records would need clearing before this code is
  deployed against it.

### P9. Claude's replies are read outside the time limit

[`attach_replies`](../../backend/timeline-api/src/routes/messages.rs#L252) reads the reply to each
row shown after the walk ends, at most 50 reads, uncounted by the time limit. The cost is fixed and
does not grow with your data, so §8b's rule holds in practice. But it is not inside the time limit,
as [O10](#o10-one-step-of-the-time-limit-is-one-row-read) first claimed.

### P10. A crash between a conversation's record and its kept branches loses the branches

Found by an agent, then checked by me in
[`write_conversation`](../../backend/timeline-api/src/processing/conversation_writer.rs#L234);
not tested.
- **The order of writes:** a new conversation's record (which lists its kept branches) is written
  first, then each branch kept as a conversation of its own.
- **The retry:** if an attempt stops between the two (for example AWS's time limit or memory
  limit), AWS retries. The retry finds a record whose source is this same upload and treats the
  conversation as done, so the branches are never written.
- **Effect:** the record then names conversations that don't exist.
- **Cheapest test:** a store that fails the first branch write once, then a retry of the upload.

### P11. Tests that check less than their names say

- **Raising the data version:** [`the_scan_raises_the_version_only_when_it_scans`](../../backend/timeline-api/tests/routes_in_parts.rs#L130)
  checks that an empty scan leaves the version alone, and that the old request form is refused.
  - It never checks that a scan which does scan raises the version. That is covered only
    indirectly, by a saved-analysis test.
- **Progress while parsing:** [`progress_is_written_while_parsing_and_a_failed_write_doesnt_stop_processing`](../../backend/timeline-api/tests/processing_paths.rs#L395)
  checks only the final progress row, not progress during parsing.
- **A missing sessions table:** [`every_session_method_reports_a_missing_table_as_a_backend_error`](../../backend/timeline-storage/tests/dynamo_sessions_and_records.rs#L108)
  checks four of the five session-store methods; `put_sessions` is not checked.
- **Flags never set:** [`getting_flags_that_were_never_set_is_404`](../../backend/timeline-api/tests/app.rs#L150)
  is unchanged and still passes, but now because the made-up message has no row, not because it has
  no flags.

### P12. Comments and names left out of date

- **`MessagesQuery`'s doc:** at [messages.rs:70](../../backend/timeline-api/src/routes/messages.rs#L70)
  it names `Filters::parse`, which does not exist; parsing is done by `MessagesQuery::filter`.

### P13. chrono-tz's licence is not recorded where it is added

chrono-tz is added in three Cargo.toml files:
- [timeline-core](../../backend/timeline-core/Cargo.toml#L13)
- [timeline-storage](../../backend/timeline-storage/Cargo.toml#L32)
- [timeline-api](../../backend/timeline-api/Cargo.toml#L42)

None of them carries a licence comment, unlike flate2 and futures. Its licence (MIT or Apache-2.0)
was checked during the work, but not written down there.

### P14. The scan's cost and its effect on other reads

Both inferred from the code by an agent; neither measured.
- **The cost:** each session the scan finishes is recounted through
  [`session_entries`](../../backend/timeline-api/src/message_query.rs#L250), which lists all your
  sessions each time. A full scan therefore makes roughly one session listing per session.
- **The effect on other reads:** the scan raises the data version on every part that scans
  anything. A page reading something else in parts at the same time would start over each time.

### P15. Small fixes and changes the page agent made without saying

- **Two fixes:**
  - The reply row in Review now spans the right number of columns (7, not 6, when the Approve
    column shows).
  - Conversation names and message ids put into HTML attributes are now escaped fully, quote marks
    included (`escapeAttribute`).
- **Two changes:**
  - The hover text for automatic flags from an "llm" source was dropped. No such source exists any
    more, so it could not show.
  - The idle-time analysis now relies on the server sending each conversation's sessions in time
    order; it used to sort them itself. The comment at
    [analyses.js:111](../../frontend/core/analyses.js#L111) states the assumption, and nothing
    checks it.

### P16. The vendored parser could not be compared with the published package

I had no network access during the check.
- **What was checked:** the checksums in [vendor/streamparser-json/README.md](../../vendor/streamparser-json/README.md)
  match the files as committed. That shows the files are unchanged since the README was written.
- **What was not:** whether they equal the published 0.0.26 package apart from the removed
  source-map lines ([O30](#o30-source-map-lines-removed-from-the-vendored-parser-page-agent)).

---

## File changes

Every file this work added, changed or removed outside `docs/`, between `3ae3c16` (the last commit before the plan's code) and `b2dc683`: 246 files. Each file has an ID (**F1**, **F2**, …) and each changed item inside it an ID (**F12.3** is file F12's third item), so you can answer one by its ID.

- **What an item is:** a function, method, type, constant, test, CSS rule, template resource or heading. Items were found by a script that reads the diff and names the item each changed line falls in. Its outline is a heuristic, so a few rows name a neighbouring item; those rows say so.
- **"(top of file)"** covers imports and the module's opening comment.
- **Vendored third-party files and `Cargo.lock`** are described as whole files.
- **Compare links** open GitHub's comparison of the two commits at that item's line. **They work only once `b2dc683` is pushed to GitHub**; on 2026-10-07, 189 commits of this work were not yet pushed. GitHub may also show very large files folded, needing a "Load diff" click before the link jumps to the line.
- **The descriptions** were written by ten Claude agents, one per group of files, each reading the diff and commit messages for its files. Where a reason is not stated in the plan, a commit message or this report, the text says "Inferred:".

#### F10. `backend/timeline-api/src/cursor.rs` (added)

New. Defines the typed cursor every request in parts hands back to the page: an enum with one variant per kind of request, sent as URL-safe base64 of a small JSON object and parsed back with a 400 naming why when it is not one this server gave. **Why:** Plan §8c: a cursor crosses a trust boundary, so it is parsed once into a typed `Cursor`; a bad cursor or one of another request kind is a 400 naming what was wrong; the user always comes from the sign-in, never the cursor.

| ID | Item | Change | What changed | Why | Compare |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F10.1 | `const MAX_CURSOR_CHARS: usize` | added | Refuses cursor text longer than 2,000 characters before decoding it. | Plan §8c and the project's rule to bound length at trust boundaries; far above any cursor the server writes. | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-4005869034838516c730539daaffd2ef97ec4fddd85e520374991e53ef93a471R23) |
| F10.2 | `enum Cursor` | added | One variant per request kind: conversations, sessions, uploads, upload-details edit (each the last item sent), and messages, files, scan and export (each a position in the message walk; export also records an open conversation and whether any was written yet). Serialized with a `kind` tag. | Plan §8c's table of requests in parts; the tag lets a cursor from one kind of request be refused by another. | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-4005869034838516c730539daaffd2ef97ec4fddd85e520374991e53ef93a471R28) |
| F10.3 | `impl Cursor` | added | Holds the encoding (`to_text`) and parsing (`parse`) of a cursor. | Plan §8c: parse once at the boundary. | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-4005869034838516c730539daaffd2ef97ec4fddd85e520374991e53ef93a471R53) |
| F10.4 | `fn to_text` | added | Encodes the cursor as JSON, then URL-safe base64 without padding. #### F15. `backend/timeline-api/src/message_query.rs` (added)

New. The one way every route reads message rows: `find_messages` lists the user's sessions, keeps those the filter admits, reads each session's rows with one range query, and hands each admitted row to a visitor, stopping at the work budget or when the visitor asks and returning a cursor to carry on from. **Why:** Plan §5b ('No route reads message rows any other way, so a fix to the reading is made once') and §8b/§8c (the shared reader gains the time limit and the cursor). Report O1 (exact time order by groups of overlapping sessions) and O10 (one step is one row read).

<a id="f16"></a>
#### F16. `backend/timeline-api/src/processing.rs` (changed)

Upload processing. It used to parse the whole file at once, store embedded reviews one by one, write one record per conversation and store later files' added messages as separate objects. It now decompresses gzip, parses the file as a stream, stores each conversation's files, message rows, sessions and record (8 conversations at a time), reports progress every second, logs each step's duration, recounts the user's totals, skips an upload already processed, and deletes the upload when done. **Why:** Plan §7 (processing steps, versioned record write, deleting the upload), §7b (gzip), §8b (progress row every second, oversize refusal), §10 step 2 and §10b (an upload already processed is skipped). Commits 2558773 and a88ccd0; report O9, O11.

<a id="f17"></a>
#### F17. `backend/timeline-api/src/processing/conversation_writer.rs` (added)

New. Writes one kept conversation: its files, message rows and sessions, then its record last with a versioned (conditional) write. If another file wins the race for the same conversation, it re-reads and redoes the work as a merge, up to 5 times; branches kept as their own conversations are written too. **Why:** Plan §7 (write order, conditional write and redo, C1), §4 (files), §4d (branches kept as conversations, revived branches), §4e (unknown times). Report B2 (a redo now brings the record in line with stored rows).

<a id="f18"></a>
#### F18. `backend/timeline-api/src/processing/upload_reader.rs` (added)

New. Reads an upload: decompresses it if it starts with gzip's marker bytes, then parses the JSON as a stream, one conversation at a time, turning each into what is kept of it as soon as it is parsed, while counting bytes read for the progress row. **Why:** Plan §7b (gzip with flate2; plain uploads still accepted per §10b), §8b (the file parsed as a stream so no step grows with the file; bytes read reported), §10 step 2.

| ID | Item | Change | What changed | Why | Compare |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F18.1 | `const GZIP_MAGIC:` | added | gzip's two marker bytes, 0x1f 0x8b. | Plan §10b: gzip is decompressed, anything else read as plain JSON. | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-5fbe9f4650b86a0d7a01acc750893f85310c82ccc6740aba5fd06b18a7e46f6eR33) |
| F18.2 | `enum ReadError` | added | Why an upload couldn't be read: decompression, invalid UTF-8, format, or a conversation that couldn't be kept (for example an unreadable review). Its own wording was removed in commit a88ccd0. | Kept separate from `ProcessingError`, which converts and words each case. | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-5fbe9f4650b86a0d7a01acc750893f85310c82ccc6740aba5fd06b18a7e46f6eR38) |

#### F20. `backend/timeline-api/src/routes/analyses.rs` (added)

New. `GET /analyses/{name}` computes the two analyses that need each message's own time, `trend` (weekly or monthly flag rate) and `time-of-day`, in the viewer's time zone, saving partial and finished results so a later request with the same options carries on or answers at once. **Why:** Plan §5c (two analyses on the server, saved with the data version) and §8c (the analysis row keeps its partial result and cursor; the next request with the same options carries on).

| ID | Item | Change | What changed | Why | Compare |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F20.1 | `struct AnalysisQuery` | added | The query: optional granularity (week or month), optional view (show switches) and a required time zone name; unknown fields are refused. | Plan §5c: the page sends its time zone's name and the view. | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-6b63405e39dab2cada74f4e1f0d4674bb9bed4d3eb16cda556b001f0171a7c15R45) |
| F20.2 | `enum AnalysisReply` | added | Either `done` with the numbers, or `working` with sessions done of total; both carry the data version. | Plan §8c: the page asks again while the answer says it is still working. | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-6b63405e39dab2cada74f4e1f0d4674bb9bed4d3eb16cda556b001f0171a7c15R55) |
| F20.3 | `fn parse` | added | Turns the name into trend (week by default) or time-of-day (404 for any other), parses the time zone with chrono-tz (a 400 quoting up to 60 characters of a bad one), and defaults the view to both switches. | Plan §5c (chrono-tz conversion; weeks by default, months on request). | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-6b63405e39dab2cada74f4e1f0d4674bb9bed4d3eb16cda556b001f0171a7c15R67) |
| F20.4 | `struct Count<` | added | The visitor holding the request and the numbers counted so far. | Plan §5c: counts are accumulated across parts. | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-6b63405e39dab2cada74f4e1f0d4674bb9bed4d3eb16cda556b001f0171a7c15R86) |
| F20.5 | `impl EntryVisitor for Count<` | added | Implements the walk's callback for counting. | Plan §5b: analyses read rows through `find_messages`. | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-6b63405e39dab2cada74f4e1f0d4674bb9bed4d3eb16cda556b001f0171a7c15R92) |
| F20.6 | `fn entry` | added | For each message, adds its time and flags to the numbers; notes are ignored. | Plan §5c: built from each message's own time. | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-6b63405e39dab2cada74f4e1f0d4674bb9bed4d3eb16cda556b001f0171a7c15R93) |

<a id="f21"></a>
#### F21. `backend/timeline-api/src/routes/conversations.rs` (changed)

`GET /conversations` used to return every record as a bare list. It now answers in parts (at most 1,000 records, within the work budget) with the total, a cursor and the data version; the file also gains `GET /conversations/{id}/files`, listing every file a conversation's messages carry. **Why:** Plan §8c (requests in parts; the reply now carries total, cursor and data version, approved in §10b), §4 and §5 (the open conversation lists its files), and report O20 (the 1,000-record cap, commit 8e7ba2d).

| ID | Item | Change | What changed | Why | Compare |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F21.1 | `(top of file)` | added | Module doc now covers both routes and their parts; imports add query and path extractors, serde, message-walk, session, user-record, cursor and budget types. | Plan §8c and §4. | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-74545db70c4f12a8236bb6f72c329f10b9ca78a83294f79573289e5885162fa7R1) |
| F21.2 | `const PAGE: usize` | added | Reads conversation records from storage 100 at a time. | Plan §5: paging through storage (fixes the old silent cut-off of `list_for_user`). | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-74545db70c4f12a8236bb6f72c329f10b9ca78a83294f79573289e5885162fa7R32) |

<a id="f22"></a>
#### F22. `backend/timeline-api/src/routes/detect.rs` (changed)

`POST /detect`, the scan. It used to rebuild 5 conversations per request from the stored upload files (offset and limit paging). It now reads your message rows through `find_messages` within the work budget, writes automatic flags per message, recounts each session it finishes, raises the data version, and answers with sessions done of total and a cursor. **Why:** Plan §8 (the scan reads rows, works within the time limit, cursor can stop inside a session), §6 (the scan recounts each session it finishes), §5c (the data version is raised by the scan), §10b (the paging test rewritten for the time budget).

<a id="f24"></a>
#### F24. `backend/timeline-api/src/routes/export.rs` (changed)

`GET /export`, the annotated download. It used to rebuild the original export from stored files, embed flags, save it to S3 and return a download address with flag handles. It now writes the file from message rows, in parts of at most 4 MB of text returned inside each reply with that part's flag handles; the last part adds conversations with no messages and closes the file. **Why:** Plan §5 ('The annotated download changes'), §8c (download in parts, each capped at 4 MB under Lambda's 6 MB limit), report O6 (download inside the reply), O12 (parent written only when known), O16 (still issues flag handles), B4 (empty conversations added), and §4e (unknown time written without `created_at`).

`GET`/`PATCH …/flags`. Both now read the message from its row (404 unless it is a stored message of yours); a save writes your flags onto the row, recounts that message's session, raises the data version, and answers with the flags, the recounted session and the version. **Why:** Plan §3 (flags on message rows), §6 (a flag save recounts its session in the same request), §5c (data version raised by every flag save), §8c (a flag save is not split), §10b ('GET …/flags kept, read from the message rows'). Test change T4 follows from it.

#### F27. `backend/timeline-api/src/routes/messages.rs` (added)

New. `GET /messages` serves Review: it parses the page's filters, walks matching rows in time order (or by conversation name for a Calendar day) within the budget, and answers with up to 50 rows (your messages with flags, handles and optionally Claude's reply; branch notes in place), the running match count, page-start cursors and a cursor to carry on. **Why:** Plan §5 and §5b (Review's filtering, sorting and paging move to the server through the shared filter), §8b/§8c (one cursor kept per page of 50; 'at least N pages' until the walk ends). Report O1-O4 and O23.

<a id="f28"></a>
#### F28. `backend/timeline-api/src/routes/metadata.rs` (changed)

The routes that list your uploaded files and edit a file's or a conversation's details. Listing files and editing a file's details now answer in parts (a cursor to carry on from, a total and the user's data version), record writes are redone when another writer changed the record first, and editing a conversation's start and end now moves a session placed by them. **Why:** Plan §8c puts GET /uploads and PUT /uploads/{id}/metadata in parts under the request time limit; §7's versioned record writes (C1) mean a write can be refused as stale; §4e places a conversation with messages of unknown time by its start and end. Commit 2558773.

#### F29. `backend/timeline-api/src/routes/sessions.rs` (added)

New route `GET /sessions`: every session of the user's with its fourteen flag counts, read from storage 200 at a time and answered in parts with a cursor, the user's total number of sessions and the data version. **Why:** Plan §5 adds `GET /sessions` so the Calendar, the Conversations tab and three analyses are drawn without messages; §6 defines the counts; §8c puts it in parts. The per-part cap came in commit 8e7ba2d (report O20).

<a id="f50"></a>
#### F50. `backend/timeline-api/tests/processing_rows.rs` (added)

New test file for upload processing under the new storage design: it uploads small exports (plain or gzip-compressed) and checks the message rows, sessions, notes, kept files, conversation records, user totals and progress that processing writes, read back through the stores or the real routes. It has no predecessor; it uses the shared helpers in `support/exports.rs` and `support/local_app.rs`. **Why:** Plan §10 step 12 asks for every step to be tested; this file covers processing as specified in §4–§4e, §7, §7b and §8b. Added in commit 25f3133; the report lists it under T14 (new tests).

| ID | Item | Change | What changed | Why | Compare |

Tests of the per-request log line. Its own hand-built router and in-memory stores were replaced by the shared local app, and the scan test now expects the scan's new logged facts. **Why:** §10b approved both changes: test routers move to the message store (setup only) and the scan's logged facts change with the scan (§8). Commit 7d35d9c.

The domain crate's manifest. The `v5` feature gives a branch kept as its own conversation a repeatable id (§4d; commit ae9b7c6).

#### F65. `backend/timeline-core/src/branches.rs` (added)

New pure module that splits a conversation tree into its kept path (from the start to the most recent message) and the branches that path replaced, counting each branch's words not repeated on the kept path. A conversation is left whole when links are missing or point outside it, or when any message's time is unknown. **Why:** §4d (replaced branches are pruned, with a note, or kept as their own conversation at 100 or more unrepeated words). Created untested in 3fde146, reworked in ae9b7c6 (shared word count), and fixed in a88ccd0 for B3/O14 (an unknown-time message was pruned as if oldest).

| ID | Item | Change | What changed | Why | Compare |

| F65.2 | `struct ReplacedBranch` | added | One replaced branch: its messages oldest first, the kept message that took its place (if any) and its count of words not repeated. | §4d: the note's wording needs these numbers. | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-e65a58bc5ea9e8d99338ed4a2f93760b84d6c18a3b09e4844c501da3204d4455R34) |
| F65.3 | `impl ReplacedBranch` | added | Holds `is_important`. | §4d. | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-e65a58bc5ea9e8d99338ed4a2f93760b84d6c18a3b09e4844c501da3204d4455R50) |

<a id="f69"></a>
#### F69. `backend/timeline-core/src/keep.rs` (added)

New pure module deciding what is kept of one parsed conversation: the kept path's messages as stored rows (text pieces with citations, file marks where files were presented, attachments, your review), a note for each replaced branch, important branches as conversations of their own, and the text of every file the export holds. Tool results, other tool calls, thinking and automatic flags from the file are dropped. **Why:** §2–§4d (what is kept), §4c (citations) and §5's statement that automatic flags are never taken from a file. Added in commit ae9b7c6; a88ccd0 adjusted it for unknown times (B3).

<a id="f70"></a>
#### F70. `backend/timeline-core/src/kept_files.rs` (added)

New pure module that replays Claude's file tool calls in a conversation (`create_file`, then `str_replace` edits) to get each file's final text, marks a file "may have been changed later" when a later command names it or when the page has marked it, and classifies files by extension for display. **Why:** §4 (files Claude wrote are kept at their replayed final text), C9 (a file changed by a command is kept at its last replayable version and marked) and §7b (the page adds the mark before dropping the commands). Added in commit ae9b7c6.

<a id="f72"></a>
#### F72. `backend/timeline-core/src/merge.rs` (added)

New pure module that works out what a later upload adds to a conversation already stored: by default only messages timed outside the stored range; or, when the file's newest messages continue a branch an earlier upload pruned, the stored rows after the branch point are replaced by a note (or moved to a conversation of their own if important) and the new path's messages added. Messages of unknown time are never added to a known conversation and are counted as skipped. **Why:** §4d (C12, revived branches), §4e (unknown times skipped and logged) and §10b's choice that a later file still adds only messages outside the stored time range (Q18). Added in commit ae9b7c6; fixed in a88ccd0 for B1/O15 (a revival must replace something).

| ID | Item | Change | What changed | Why | Compare |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F72.1 | `struct MovedBranch` | added | Stored messages moved into a conversation of their own because a revived branch replaced them and they hold 100 or more unrepeated words, re-keyed under the new conversation. | §4d: an important replaced path is kept as its own conversation, also when the replacing happens on a later upload. | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-036805691affbbd7ad68286532e7d4c1e1947f86046e802ab49f6849f0c3cb82R36) |

<a id="f73"></a>
#### F73. `backend/timeline-core/src/message_filter.rs` (added)

New pure module (no storage) holding Review's filters as one typed value, `MessageFilter`: conversation, time span, flag menu, search text and which flags are shown. It answers whether a stored session can hold a match and whether one stored entry matches. **Why:** Plan §5b: one filter shared by every route that reads messages, so "flagged" and the other filters mean the same everywhere; the rules are the page's `getFilteredHumanMessages`, moved to the server. First written untested in 3fde146, then extended in 53491ed for messages of unknown time (§4e), Calendar-day spans and notes.

<a id="f81"></a>
#### F81. `backend/timeline-core/src/ports/messages.rs` (added)

New port for stored message rows and branch notes, with your flags on them. It defines a range of rows to read, a reader, a whole-row writer for processing, and two narrow flag writers so the scan and a flag save can each touch only their own flags. **Why:** Plan §3 (message rows keyed by conversation, time and id; flags as separate attributes, written through `AutoFlagWriter` and `UserFlagWriter`), §5b (one range query per session) and §8c (reads that resume after a key). Replaces the `MessageFlags` port; commit 53491ed.

<a id="f86"></a>
#### F86. `backend/timeline-core/src/server_analyses.rs` (added)

New module for the two analyses the server computes from each message's own time: flag rate over time (week or month buckets) and time of day / day of week, in the viewer's time zone, with types for the saved and partly computed results. **Why:** Plan §5c: these two need each message's local time and move to the server (from the page's `computeTrendAnalysis` and `computeTimeOfDayAnalysis`), with chrono-tz for time zones; §8c: they can stop part-way and carry on. Commit 53491ed; the commit 2e49e5b says the week rule was checked against the page's own code run in Node.

#### F87. `backend/timeline-core/src/stored_message.rs` (added)

New module for what is kept of a conversation's messages: each kept message as a row with its text pieces and citations, marks for files it presented, attachments, and your flags; and a note row for each replaced branch. **Why:** Plan §2–§4d (what is kept: text, citations, file references, parent links, replaced-branch notes) and §3 (row key of conversation, time and id). First written untested in 3fde146; 53491ed made the key's time readable as a `MessageTime` (§4e).

New module for a stored session: the fourteen counts, how its start and end were decided, its key, and the functions that cut a conversation's entries into sessions or place it as one session by its start and end. **Why:** Plan §3 and §6 (session rows with fourteen counts), §4d (notes count as activity) and §4e (a conversation with any message of unknown time is one session placed by its record's span). First written untested in 3fde146; 53491ed added `Placement`, `SessionKey` and `sessions_for`.

#### F89. `backend/timeline-core/src/walk_cursor.rs` (added)

New module with `WalkCursor`, the typed form of where a walk over the user's messages stopped: the group of sessions it was in and the last entry done in it. **Why:** Plan §8c: each partial answer carries a cursor naming where to carry on; report O1 (sessions are walked in groups whose time spans overlap, so Review's time order is exact). #### F90. `backend/timeline-core/src/work_budget.rs` (added)

New module for the work budget: what a request asks before each step, answered by a 9-second clock in production or by a step count in tests. **Why:** Plan §8b and §8c: every long loop stops at a time limit and reports progress; tests count steps so they can stop after exactly N steps whatever the computer's speed. Commit 53491ed; `unlimited` added in ae9b7c6.

#### F104. `backend/timeline-core/tests/work_budget.rs` (added)

New test file for `WorkBudget`, the value each server loop asks "may I do another step?": by counting steps in tests, by the clock in production, or without limit. **Why:** §8c makes the per-request time limit testable through a budget that counts steps in tests and uses a 9-second clock in production. Added in commit 2e49e5b; commit 25f3133 added the unlimited-budget test.

| ID | Item | Change | What changed | Why | Compare |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| F104.2 | `fn a_clock_budget_allows_the_first_step_and_none_once_its_time_is_up` | added | Checks that a clock budget with no time still allows the first step, then none. | Inferred from the doc comment: every request makes progress, so a carry-on loop can't stall. | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-19631548c89288d3abf0b5ee8393280f35aa90a4b6424493b26dbdcbad6b335cR22) |

<a id="f111"></a>
#### F111. `backend/timeline-storage/src/dynamo/message_rows.rs` (added)

New DynamoDB adapter for message and note rows in the conversations table, keyed `MSG#{conversation}#{time}#{id}` so a session's rows are one run of keys; your flags are stored on your message rows in separate automatic and your-own attributes. **Why:** §3 (messages as rows, flags on them, the time in the key) and §4e (unknown time as the zero date); replaces the `MessageFlags` table. Commit 5380240.

<a id="f112"></a>
#### F112. `backend/timeline-storage/src/dynamo/query.rs` (added)

New helper module with one function that reads every row a DynamoDB query matches, following DynamoDB's carry-on key past each 1 MB answer. **Why:** §5: each request pages past DynamoDB's 1 MB per call, which also fixes the silent cut-off of `list_for_user`. Commit 5380240.

| ID | Item | Change | What changed | Why | Compare |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F112.1 | `fn query_all` | added | Runs a query repeatedly from an optional start key until DynamoDB reports no more rows, or until at least `enough` rows have arrived; a failed call is a reported backend error. | §5 and §8c (reads in parts start after a cursor key and stop at a part's size). | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-d9fb6e60ba0809a9aac6f088bb5106795b4f8410fb20aaeec798a42a707b5851R18) |

<a id="f113"></a>
#### F113. `backend/timeline-storage/src/dynamo/sessions_table.rs` (added)

New DynamoDB adapter for session rows in the conversations table, keyed `SESS#{conversation}#{number}` with the session held as JSON. **Why:** §3 and §6: sessions are stored with their fourteen counts so the page draws the Calendar without reading messages. Commit 5380240.

#### F114. `backend/timeline-storage/src/dynamo/user_record_rows.rs` (added)

New DynamoDB adapter for the user's own record (sort key `USER`: data version and totals) and saved analyses (`ANALYSIS#…`), both in the conversations table. **Why:** §5c (data version, saved analyses), §8b (totals for the progress bar) and choice O5 (a new `USER` row, since no user record existed). <a id="f116"></a>
#### F116. `backend/timeline-storage/src/memory/conversations.rs` (changed)

The in-memory conversation-record store now keeps records in key order, reads them a page at a time, and refuses a write whose version is stale, as the DynamoDB adapter does. **Why:** §7 and C1 (versioned writes) and §8c (records in parts); the in-memory store must pass the same contract as DynamoDB. Commit 5380240.

| ID | Item | Change | What changed | Why | Compare |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| F116.2 | `struct InMemoryConversationSummaryStore` | changed | The map of records is now a `BTreeMap`, ordered by user and conversation id. | Pages must come back in a stable key order, as DynamoDB's do. | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-61919af814507ae799cf4de421052bc1d489a276a6160827a38c3b24788e26afR14) |
| F116.3 | `fn new` | changed | Unchanged. <a id="f118"></a>
#### F118. `backend/timeline-storage/src/memory/messages.rs` (added)

New in-memory message store: keeps each user's message rows (your messages with their flags, Claude's replies, and notes where a replaced branch was pruned) in a sorted map keyed by user and entry key (conversation, time, message id). It implements the reading, row-writing, automatic-flag and review-flag traits on one struct, and replaces the in-memory store of the removed MessageFlags port (`InMemoryMessageFlagsStore`). **Why:** Plan §3 moves messages into rows with their flags on them and removes the MessageFlags table; plan §10 step 1 asks for in-memory and DynamoDB adapters of the new ports (commit 5380240). The in-memory store backs the local server and the shared contract tests.

<a id="f127"></a>
#### F127. `backend/timeline-storage/tests/dynamo_message_rows.rs` (added)

New tests of `DynamoMessageStore` (message rows with flags, in the conversations table) against DynamoDB Local: the shared message-row contract, rows the code didn't write, a missing table, flag attributes of the wrong type, reading past DynamoDB's 1 MB per answer, and, against a stand-in server, batches DynamoDB hands back unfinished. **Why:** Plan §10b replaces `dynamo_message_flags.rs` test for test; plan §7 requires resending unfinished batches up to 5 tries and then failing with a count of rows left; plan §5 requires paging past 1 MB. Commit 2e49e5b.

#### F131. `backend/timeline-storage/tests/support/conversation_summary_contract.rs` (changed)

The conversation-record contract (run on both the in-memory and DynamoDB stores) now builds records with the new fields, expects each write to return the record with its version raised by one, replaces the "put again replaces" test with a versioned-write test, and adds a test of the paged listing. **Why:** Plan §10b approved turning `put_again_replaces_the_earlier_summary` into "a write with the version read replaces it; a stale one is refused" (§7, C1); plan §8c's `GET /conversations` in parts needs a paged listing. Commit 2e49e5b.

| ID | Item | Change | What changed | Why | Compare |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F131.1 | `fn summary` | changed | The contract's record builder gains `version: 0`, `untimed: 0`, `branch_of: None` and empty `branches`. | The record type gained these fields (§4d, §4e, §7). | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-eb7441d8daeaac1b1c9156a486b8290a6b093145847f645c731ed486dfdfbafaR30) |

| F131.3 | `fn put_then_get_round_trips_every_field` | changed | Now also sets `untimed` and both branch fields, and checks `put` returns, and `get` reads back, the record with version raised. | So every new field is round-tripped (§4d, §4e) and the version rule of §7 is checked. | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-eb7441d8daeaac1b1c9156a486b8290a6b093145847f645c731ed486dfdfbafaR90) |

<a id="f132"></a>
#### F132. `backend/timeline-storage/tests/support/fake_dynamodb.rs` (added)

New test helper: a tiny local HTTP server that speaks just enough of DynamoDB's protocol for the real AWS client to talk to it, and answers every batch write by handing back some or all rows as unprocessed, as DynamoDB does when busy. **Why:** Plan §7 requires resending unfinished batches and failing after 5 tries; DynamoDB Local never hands rows back, so without the stand-in that path could not be tested through the adapters' public methods (commit 2e49e5b message).

| ID | Item | Change | What changed | Why | Compare |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F132.1 | `enum Busy` | added | How the stand-in answers: hand back every row always, or only for the first n answers. | Lets one test cover "resent then succeeds" and another "still unfinished after every try". | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-2b8c11c077697e67348118ddc8c3e663bb1c8e3145e81a485b2a8154f5bc372eR20) |
| F132.2 | `struct FakeDynamo` | added | A running stand-in: a real DynamoDB client pointed at it, and a shared count of the batch-write calls it answered. | Tests assert the number of tries from the call count. | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-2b8c11c077697e67348118ddc8c3e663bb1c8e3145e81a485b2a8154f5bc372eR28) |
| F132.3 | `fn start` | added | Binds a local port, starts accepting connections in the background, and builds a DynamoDB client with test credentials aimed at that port. | Setup for the resend tests. | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-2b8c11c077697e67348118ddc8c3e663bb1c8e3145e81a485b2a8154f5bc372eR33) |
| F132.4 | `fn serve` | added | Reads HTTP requests on one connection (headers, then the body by its stated length), counts each call, and answers with the request's rows as `UnprocessedItems` or with none, per the `Busy` setting. | The minimum of DynamoDB's protocol the SDK client needs for `BatchWriteItem`. | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-2b8c11c077697e67348118ddc8c3e663bb1c8e3145e81a485b2a8154f5bc372eR62) |

<a id="f134"></a>
#### F134. `backend/timeline-storage/tests/support/message_rows_contract.rs` (added)

New shared contract every message-row store must pass (run on the in-memory store and on DynamoDB Local): round trips of every kind of row (your messages with flags, Claude's replies with citations, notes), the automatic/review flag separation, range and cursor reads, finding by id, the reply after a message, deletes, isolation between users, and more rows than one DynamoDB batch. **Why:** Plan §10b replaces the MessageFlags contract and its in-memory and DynamoDB tests one for one, each replacement naming the test it replaces; plan §3 puts flags on message rows, §5b reads by span, §8c carries on after a cursor (commit 2e49e5b).

No longer cuts sessions from messages. It now turns each session from `GET /sessions` into the page's drawing form (`toBlock`), keeps the local-day helpers, and adds `localDayBounds` to send a Calendar day to the server. **Why:** Plan §3: sessions are cut on the server (and placed by start and end for messages of unknown time, §4e); which local day a session falls on stays in the browser. §10b removed the page tests of cutting and placing. New module that inserts numbered citation markers into a reply's raw text at the end of each cited span, and decides which cited addresses may become links. **Why:** Plan §4c: Review shows a small numbered link after each cited span; positions refer to the raw text, so markers go in before Markdown formatting. Commit 1e018c9.

New module that reads a request the server answers in parts: follows each part's cursor to the end, and starts over (up to three times) if the user's data version changes between parts. **Why:** Plan §8c: answers carry a cursor and the data version; a changed version means data changed underneath, so the page starts that request over and says so. Commit 1e018c9.

| ID | Item | Change | What changed | Why | Compare |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F154.1 | `MAX_RESTARTS` | added | New: 3, how many times a reading starts over before failing. | Not in the plan. Inferred: so data that keeps changing can't keep the page reading forever (the comment's stated reason). | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-5564d912ef3ef6a3f4fb8c607161e972d585ea7b27ed2a91e25219958e84937dR14) |
| F154.2 | `readAllParts` | added | New: repeats a full reading until one completes with a single data version, calling `onRestart` between attempts, and throws a readable error after the last restart. | Plan §8c ("Your data changed; starting again"). | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-5564d912ef3ef6a3f4fb8c607161e972d585ea7b27ed2a91e25219958e84937dR20) |
| F154.3 | `readOnce` | added | New (module-private): one reading from the start, returning null as soon as a part's data version differs from the first part's. | Plan §8c. | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-5564d912ef3ef6a3f4fb8c607161e972d585ea7b27ed2a91e25219958e84937dR32) |
| F154.4 | `joinParts` | added | New: concatenates one field (for example `conversations`) across all parts. | Plan §8c: the page keeps the records and sessions received so far. | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-5564d912ef3ef6a3f4fb8c607161e972d585ea7b27ed2a91e25219958e84937dR46) |

<a id="f155"></a>
#### F155. `frontend/core/review-query.js` (added)

New module that builds Review's query to `GET /messages` from its filters, and keeps, between parts, only the match count and each page of 50's starting cursor. **Why:** Plan §5b (Review's filters run on the server) and §8c (the page keeps for each page of 50 its starting cursor; "at least N pages" until the walk ends). Commit 1e018c9.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| F155.3 | `partQuery` | added | New: adds where to carry on (cursor, rows and notes matched so far), how many rows are wanted, and whether to stop when they are there or keep counting. | The request shape of report O2. | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-4503e8bcf76b9ffdc533ff24c4b4688d6a03a081a30d5892e3de7cca3ef467eaR30) |

<a id="f158"></a>
#### F158. `frontend/core/slim-export.js` (added)

New module that slims an export, one conversation at a time, before it is sent: keeps only what the server uses (ids, names, times, parents, senders, attachments, file references, your reviews, text pieces with citations, and the tool calls that write or present files) and drops the rest. It builds the slimmed file's text in the same outer shape as the original. **Why:** Plan §7b: a 63.5 MB export becomes about 9 MB (2.8 MB compressed), so sending takes about 1 s instead of 26 s. Called from the upload worker (`workers/slim-stream.js`). Commit 1e018c9.

| F158.2 | `CONVERSATION_FIELDS` | added | New: the conversation fields kept (id, name, created and updated times). | Plan §7b's kept list. | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-20a6ca1fcc9ac74790d759b19fa1b259b8de4b747a6212c31144215b51755b3dR26) |

<a id="f160"></a>
#### F160. `frontend/core/turns.js` (added)

New module that runs a long piece of page work in turns: a generator yields after each step, each turn runs steps until its budget says stop, reports progress and hands the screen back. A stopped generator can be resumed later. **Why:** Plan §8b: drawing the timeline and the page analyses hand the screen back every 50 ms, reporting each time, so the bar keeps moving; §8c: analyses carry on where they stopped. Commit 1e018c9.

| ID | Item | Change | What changed | Why | Compare |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F160.1 | `runInTurns` | added | New: loops turns until the generator finishes (resolving with its result) or `stopped()` is true before a turn (resolving unfinished, leaving the generator where it is). Every turn does at least one step. | Plan §8b (time-limited loops, one step between clock checks) and §8c (stop and carry on). | [diff](https://github.com/Telotrope/conversation-timeline/compare/3ae3c16ba50676a0b70788d297db485c45127473...b2dc6831443785b8e6872b444671cff15b7e97db#diff-a6b4fb665091f1d8994a7004f83591e6085bc1354926c833ae958ed74d4e7eb1R20) |

New page unit tests of `core/parts.js`, which reads an answer given in parts: asking with each cursor until none is returned, starting over when the data version changes, and giving up after a few restarts. **Why:** §8c: answers come in parts with a cursor and the data version; a changed version starts the request over. #### F196. `frontend/tests/slim-stream.test.js` (added)

New page unit tests for the upload worker's pipeline (`workers/slim-stream.js`): a file read as a stream, parsed one conversation at a time with the vendored @streamparser/json parser, slimmed (stripped of what the server does not keep) and gzip-compressed, with progress reports. It runs the real pipeline in Node, with only the clock replaced. **Why:** Plan §7b (slim the file in the browser before sending) and §8b (preparing the file reports every 0.5 s); step 8 of §10. Added in commit 1e018c9 by the page agent (report T14).

New page unit tests for the Upload page's steps (ui/load-flow.js): each file prepared in a stand-in worker and sent slimmed, or as it is; one progress bar across the batch; the scan asked again with its cursor until done; and files sent in their order. **Why:** Plan §7b, §8 and §8b; step 11 of §10. Added in commit 8757068 by the page agent; the last test and the worker delay were added in commit a1635fe for bug B7 (report T2, T14).

New page unit tests for the work budgets (core/work-budget.js) that every waiting loop asks between steps: a clock budget and a step-counting budget. **Why:** Plan §8c ("How the time limit is made testable"): the real budget answers by the clock, the tests' one by counting steps.
